<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par114 />examples, {{GHGpar|111|g}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=27}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּֽהְיוֹתָם בְּמִצְרַ֫יִם|translate=when they were in Egypt}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=30}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי כִרְאֹת אֶת־הַנֶּ֫זֶם... וּכְשָׁמְעוֹ וג׳|translate=and it came to pass, when he saw}} (prop. in the seeing) ''the ring''..., ''and when he heard'' (prop. in his hearing), &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|f}}
But by far the most frequent is the connexion of the infinitive construct with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}.<ref>Cf. {{GHGpar|45|g}}, according to which the close union of the {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} with the first consonant of the infinitive ({{GHGheb|text=לִכְתֹּב}} with a firmly closed syllable, as opposed to {{GHGheb|text=בִּכְתֹב}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּכְתֹב}}, &c.) seems to point to the formation of a special new verbal form. Quite distinct are the few examples where the infinitive with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} serves to express time, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=63}} {{GHGheb|text=לִפְנוֹת עָ֫רֶב|translate=at the eventide}} (prop. at the time of the return of evening); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=23|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=26}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=29}} ''when Joab sent the king’s servant''.</ref> Starting from the fundamental meaning of {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, i.e. ''direction towards something'', infinitives with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} serve to express the most varied ideas of purpose or aim, and very commonly also (with a weakening or a complete disregard of the original meaning of the {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}) to introduce the object of an action, or finally even (like the infinitive absolute used adverbially, {{GHGpar|113|h}}, and the Latin gerund in ''-ndo'') to state motives or attendant circumstances. See the instances in the Remarks.

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|g}}
Rem. 1. The original meaning of the {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is most plainly seen in those infinitives with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} which expressly state a purpose (hence as the equivalent of a final clause), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=5}} ''and the Lord came down'', {{GHGheb|text=לִרְאֹת אֶת־הָעִיר|translate=to see the city}}; also with a change of subject, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=10}} ''and thou hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite'' {{GHGheb|text=לִֽהְיוֹת לְךָ לְאִשָּׁה|translate=to be}} (i.e. that she may be) ''thy wife''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=26}} ({{GHGheb|text=לָמוּת}}).—If there is a special emphasis on the infinitive with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, it is placed, with its complement, before the governing verb, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=2}} with {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹא}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=25}} with {{GHGheb|text=עָלָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|h}}
2. Just as clearly the idea of aiming at a definite purpose or turning towards an object may be seen in the combination of the verb {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה|translate=to be}}, with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} and an infinitive. In fact {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה לַֽעֲשׂוֹת}} may mean, either (''a'') ''he was in the act of, he was about to'' (as it were, he set himself), ''he was ready, to do'' something, or (''b'') ''he'' or it ''was appointed'' or ''compelled'', &c., to do the action in question. In the latter case {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה לַֽעֲשׂוֹת}} corresponds to the Latin ''faciendum erat'', cf. also the English ''I am to go''. In both cases {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה}} (as elsewhere when copula) is often omitted.

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|i}}
Examples of (''a'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי הַשֶּׁ֫מֶשׁ לָבוֹא|translate=and when the sun was going down}} (just about to set); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=26|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי לִדְרשׁ אֱלֹהִים|translate=and he set himself to seek God}} (here with the secondary idea of a continuous action); with the omission of {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=20}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְהֹוָה לְהֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֫נִי|translate=the Lord}} is ready ''to save me''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=21}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=49}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=25|verse=14}} (''et foedus suum manifestaturus est eis''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=18|verse=24}} (?), 19:8 ({{GHGheb|text=לִמְצֹא|translate=consecuturus}}<section end=par114 /><noinclude>
